acknowledge.text: Something is pulling at you. It's allowed to be here while you look after yourself.
Your guard is up a little. Let's give your body a moment before anything else.
That sounds like a lot to hold. You noticed it, and that's a good place to start.
This is a lot right now. You don't have to sort it out this minute.
Your body is on high alert. Let's slow just one thing down: your breath.

understand.text: Tension often comes with energy your body has made to deal with something: a quicker heartbeat, tight shoulders, busy thoughts. It's usually trying to protect you, even when there's nothing to fight.
Many people find that settling the body first makes their thoughts easier to sort out afterwards.

options.title: Breathe out longer than in
options.text: Breathe in gently, then let the out-breath be a little longer. Follow the circle for a few rounds.
options.why: Longer out-breaths often help the body ease out of alert mode.

options.title: Five things you can see
options.text: Look around and name five things you can see, four you can touch, three you can hear, two you can smell, one you can taste.
options.why: Naming what's around you brings your attention back to the present, where things are often more manageable.

options.title: Tense and let go
options.text: Squeeze your hands, then your shoulders, for a moment each, and let them drop.
options.why: Tightening on purpose and then letting go can help you notice, and release, tension you're already holding.

options.title: Put it in one sentence
options.text: Finish this: "I'm tense because…". It doesn't have to be fair or reasonable, just true.
options.why: Putting a feeling into words can make it a little quieter.

options.title: Park the worry
options.text: Write down what's worrying you and pick a time later today to come back to it. Until then, it's parked.
options.why: Many people find that a set time for worrying makes it easier to let it rest in between.
options.prompt: What's worrying you? Write it here, and come back to it later.

options.title: Yours, or not yours?
options.text: Split what's on your mind in two: the parts you can do something about, and the parts you can't.
options.why: Seeing which parts are in your hands often makes the next step clearer, and the rest easier to set aside.
options.prompt: What's in my hands here, and what isn't?

options.title: Move it through
options.text: A short walk, even just to the end of the street and back. Or a few shoulder rolls where you are.
options.why: Tense energy often wants to move. Giving it somewhere to go can help it settle.

options.title: Change what you hear
options.text: Put on rain or waves and let it fill the room for a while.
options.why: A steady, gentle sound can give a busy mind something softer to rest on.

options.title: Talk about anything
options.text: Message or call someone you're comfortable with. It doesn't have to be about this.
options.why: An ordinary conversation can remind your body that you're not on your own.

options.title: Empty your head
options.text: Write down everything on your mind, in any order. Nobody will read it.
options.why: Getting thoughts onto a page often makes them feel less tangled.
options.prompt: Everything on my mind right now:

options.title: Talk to someone now
options.text: If this feels like too much on your own, there are people you can talk to, any time.
options.why: You don't have to carry this by yourself.
